title: Stream choreography: SDK-side contract and resumable handshake (scratchpad)
content:
Objective:

Draft the SDK-facing contract and runtime choreography for incremental/streamed responses that may include tool calls and structured frames, with first-class resume semantics for flaky networks and client restarts. This doc is a scratchpad: design notes, example traffic, trade-offs, and open questions for the hosted-api streaming PRD workstream.

Context / motivation:
- Customers embed streaming LLM outputs into interactive UIs (chat widgets, copilots). They expect low first-byte latency and the ability to recover mid-response when networks drop.
- Tool-calling introduces extra boundaries: intermediate tool results should be surfaced, optionally executed by clients, and included in resume semantics.
- Current SDK patterns at Redwood are oriented to whole-response semantics or naive chunking; we need a clearer contract that balances developer ergonomics, server resources (batching/prefetch), and observable consistency.

Goals (MVP):
1) A minimal SDK handshake that establishes a resumable session id and protocol version.
2) Incremental framed output where each frame is typed (text, action/tool-call, structured-json, checkpoint) and self-describing enough for client replay.
3) Resume semantics that allow a client to reconnect, indicate which frames it already has, and receive the remainder without server-side duplicate tool invocations.
4) Backpressure and prefetch knobs in the SDK for low-latency UIs and bandwidth-constrained devices.
5) Clear telemetry points for debugging partial failures and tool call latencies.

Actors and primitives (informal):
- session_id: server-assigned, canonical for resume. TTL policy (default 24h for hosted API; configurable for Dedicated).
- frame: atomic incremental unit. fields: frame_id (monotonic per-session), type, payload, signature (optional), sequence_hash (for quick diff).
- frame types: TEXT_CHUNK, TOOL_CALL_START, TOOL_CALL_RESULT, STRUCTURED_OBJECT, CHECKPOINT, END.
- client_offset: client advertises last_frame_id it persisted on reconnect. Server uses this to stream only frames > client_offset.
- durable-tool-token: tokenized handle to avoid re-executing expensive tool calls on resume. Server keeps tool outputs keyed by tool_call_id while session active.

High-level flow examples:
1) Normal streaming (no tools):
  - Client POST /v1/responses?stream=true -> server returns HTTP 200 and a JSON prelude containing session_id, proto_version, first_frame_id.
  - Server sends frames: TEXT_CHUNK(f1), TEXT_CHUNK(f2), CHECKPOINT(f3), END(f4).
  - Client acknowledges checkpoints optionally (ACK frames over a side channel / websockets) for weaker consistency guarantees.

2) Tool call inside stream:
  - Server emits TOOL_CALL_START(f5, tool_spec), then pauses that logical slot until tool result ready.
  - If tool is executed server-side, avoid re-run on resume: server persists TOOL_CALL_RESULT with tool_call_id and marks slot complete.
  - If tool is intended for client execution (client-side toollet), server may emit TOOL_CALL_START with a client_invoke hint; resume must not re-emit start if client already executed and returned a result slot.

3) Reconnect / resume:
  - Client reconnects and does POST /v1/resume with session_id, last_frame_seen=7.
  - Server returns remaining frames and a mapping of tool_call_ids -> status (complete / pending / failed). If tool_call pending and server-side, server may block for a bounded time or emit an interim status frame.

Design details and choices:
- Framing format: JSON lines (ndjson) vs compact binary proto. MVP: ndjson to maximize debuggability and client integration speed. Consider a Protobuf v2 in a follow-up for mobile perf.

- Checkpoint semantics: CHECKPOINT frames are server-driven and recommended to be placed after key logical boundaries (e.g., after first complete paragraph, after tool result). Clients may persist to local cache upon seeing a checkpoint. Checkpoints are the unit of resume acknowledgment; partial text frames may be replayed from offset within a checkpoint (rare).

- Idempotency and tool calls: assign tool_call_id (UUID). Server guarantees at-most-once semantics for server-executed tool calls while session state exists. If a client reconnects and indicates it lacks frames that include the tool result, server will re-send stored result rather than re-run. After session TTL elapses, server may garbage collect tool outputs and re-run if requested (documented).

- Prefetch and latency budget: clients can send preferred_latency_budget_ms in the initial handshake. Server attempts to favor low-latency execution (smaller batches) for sessions with tight budgets but may degrade throughput/cost. A recommended mapping: <50ms => favor synchronous low-batch; 50–200ms => small batching; >200ms => max batching. This is advisory and can be overridden by server-side policies.

- Backpressure and windowing: for websocket clients we expose a sliding window: client_window_frames (N) to limit server pushing; server respects and will not exceed outstanding frames without ACK. For HTTP streaming we use a simple token bucket delivered as CHECKPOINT ACKS (client polls ACK).

SDK ergonomics (surface, examples):
- JS (browser) minimal pattern:
  const res = await client.responses.create({ prompt, stream: true });
  res.on('frame', frame => { switch(frame.type) { case 'TEXT_CHUNK': appendText(frame.payload); break; case 'TOOL_CALL_START': showToolPreview(frame.payload); break; case 'CHECKPOINT': persistCheckpoint(frame.frame_id); break; }});
  res.on('disconnect', () => { storeLastFrameId(sessionId, lastSeen); });
  // resume
  const r2 = await client.responses.resume({ session_id, last_frame_seen });

- SDK should surface helpers: autoResume(client, session_id), checkpointPersistenceStrategy (in-memory/localStorage/indexeddb), and a ToolAdapter interface for client-executed tools.

Telemetry and SLOs:
- Track first-byte latency, median frame delta, tool_call_latency, resume_success_rate, duplicate-tool-run-rate.
- SLO targets (hosted): 95th first-byte < 200ms for low-latency sessions; resume_success_rate > 99% within session TTL.

Open questions / trade-offs to resolve:
1) Should checkpoints be client-acknowledged synchronously or eventually? (trade: stronger resume vs bandwidth/latency)
2) How long to retain server-side tool results for at-most-once semantics (default 24h?) and how to surface GC semantics to customers?
3) Should we allow partial resume within a TEXT_CHUNK (byte offsets) to support huge single-chunk frames? (adds complexity; prefer chunking strategy instead)
4) How to represent structured output versions (schema evolution): attach schema_version to STRUCTURED_OBJECT frames and provide a schema registry URL in prelude.
5) Mobile optimizations: binary encoding, compressed frames, optional resumable-diff frames to reduce replay cost.

Security / privacy notes:
- Tool outputs may include PII; session TTL and retention policies must be configurable per-customer (Dedicated/Private).
- All resume requests must be authenticated and authorized for the session token; short-lived ephemeral session tokens should be supported for browser clients.

Next concrete steps (short-term):
- (Ethan) Draft wire protocol spec for ndjson frames (schema for each frame type). Target: 2026-03-19.
- (Priya) Prototype SDK JS helper autoResume + local checkpoint persistence. Target: 2026-04-02.
- (Marco) Server PoC: session store model, tool_call_id lifecycle, TTL GC behavior. Target: 2026-04-09.
- (Sofia) Telemetry dashboard mockups and list of metrics. Target: 2026-03-26.

Decision checkpoints for PRD (milestones):
- Protocol spec agreed and reviewed (engineering + SDK) -> lock framing for MVP.
- Security/retention knobs documented for enterprise customers -> policy fields in API.
- End-to-end demo (browser + hosted API) showing resume after network drop with tool call preserved.

Appendix: quick example stream (ndjson lines):
{"session_id":"sess_01F...", "proto":"v0.1", "first_frame": 1}
{"frame_id":1, "type":"TEXT_CHUNK", "payload":"Hello"}
{"frame_id":2, "type":"TEXT_CHUNK", "payload":" world"}
{"frame_id":3, "type":"TOOL_CALL_START", "payload":{"tool":"search", "q":"redwood inference latency paper"}, "tool_call_id":"t-abc123"}
{"frame_id":4, "type":"TOOL_CALL_RESULT", "tool_call_id":"t-abc123", "payload":{"items": [...]} }
{"frame_id":5, "type":"CHECKPOINT"}
{"frame_id":6, "type":"END"}

Notes: this doc intentionally mixes high-level PRD threads with engineering todo's. Use this as the living scratchpad when we triage API-1234/PR-482. Update the linked artifacts as concrete PRs and RFCs land.

Unresolved: who owns session TTL config in product APIs (product vs infra)? pinging @product-hosted-api in Slack thread.
